messages:
maria: quick follow-up on yesterday's conversation — proposing a small convergence on SDK retry + pagination ergonomics across py/ts/go. want to check tradeoffs before i write an RFC.

kevin: nice. what's the concrete ask? unify API shapes or runtime behaviors?

maria: both. problem: each language picked subtly different defaults for resume tokens, prefetch, and retry window. that makes client behavior non-deterministic under transient infra errors. e.g. py auto-prefetch=3, ts prefetch=1, go no-prefetch. also backoff config lives in transport for py/ts but in connector for go.

jen: can you sketch the ideal surface?

maria: high level: 1) a single canonical retry model (idempotency + retry-window semantics) exposed in SDKs; 2) an optional "resume token" opaque string consumers can persist; 3) a small set of knobs exposed consistently: max_inflight_pages, prefetch, retry_policy (enum), resume_behavior (auto|manual).

ankit: enum for retry_policy = {standard, aggressive, none}? and what do those mean exactly?

maria: standard = exponential backoff with jitter and per-page lease awareness; aggressive = tighter retry with shorter max backoff; none = fail fast. importantly standard must account for non-idempotent streaming ops and fall back to canary-models or other backends instead of blind retry.

kevin: how do we handle streaming vs paged transports? we have a lot of code that assumes streaming is "resume-unfriendly" because we can't rehydrate KV cache.

maria: proposal: treat two orthogonal axes: transport (stream vs paged) and continuation token semantics (opaque resume token vs cursor-based stable page id). SDKs should expose the same high-level flags but doc differences for each transport. for streaming: resume_behavior defaults to manual (developer opt-in) and SDK provides a helper to convert last-seen marker -> resume token when runtime supports it.

leo: code example?

maria: here is a minimal sketch (pseudo):

```python
# python
resp = client.list_items(prefetch=2, retry_policy="standard", resume_behavior="auto")
for page in resp:
    process(page.items)
    if page.resume_token:
        save_checkpoint(page.resume_token)
```

```ts
// ts
const it = client.listItems({ prefetch: 2, retryPolicy: 'standard' });
for await (const page of it) {
  process(page.items);
  if (page.resumeToken) saveCheckpoint(page.resumeToken);
}
```

```go
// go
it := client.ListItems(ctx, ListOptions{ Prefetch: 2, RetryPolicy: RetryStandard })
for it.Next() {
  page := it.Page()
  process(page.Items)
  if page.ResumeToken != "" { saveCheckpoint(page.ResumeToken) }
}
```

jen: that looks similar across languages which is good. Daniel's team will complain about adding prefetch to the surface because of cost / memory concerns.

maria: understood — default prefetch should be conservative (1). prefetch=0 means strictly sequential. we should provide a runtime suggestion API (redwood.optimize.suggest(prefetch, quant_profile)) so consumers get a recommendation based on workload.

ankit: what about retries that cross pages? say request for page N fails after items were partially processed. do we retry page N or return an error so client handles dedup?

kevin: need to define strong idempotency guarantees. server: attach monotonic page ids + opaque resume token which includes the last-ack'ed offset. client: when retrying, include resume token to ask server for the next unserved item. default retry should only apply if resume token exists or request is idempotent.

maria: exactly. fallback policy: if no resume token, SDK should not attempt silent retry for non-idempotent ops; instead bubble error with metadata describing safe retry hints. small helper `isRetrySafe(err)` in SDKs.

leo: ergonomics question: Should we surface resume_token as a property on the page or on iterator state? differing placement in libs has caused confusion.

maria: put it on the page object to make checkpointing explicit. iterator.state.resume_token is second-class and might confuse users who use manual iteration.

kevin: tests: need integration tests simulating partial pages + leader failover. We should add chaos tests to the SDK harness that assert no duplicates under standard policy.

maria: yep. accept criteria for RFC: 1) API sketches for py/ts/go (including defaults) 2) transport compatibility matrix (stream/paged) 3) server-side contract for resume token contents (opaque, monotonic offset) 4) test plan + opt-in runtime suggestions hook.

jen: timeline?

maria: aiming for RFC next week, PRs the week after. small backwards-compatible shim layer in each SDK to map old flags -> new unified flags.

ankit: one more: telemetry. we need per-page metrics: fetch_latency, retries_count, resume_used boolean. can we add token-level telemetry (redact token) so optimize can learn prefs?

maria: yes — add telemetry events: page_fetch(start/end), resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_fallback. tokens must never be logged raw, only token-hash or length.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: none — informational thread. :white_check_mark:

kevin: feel free to ping me once you have the RFC draft. i can prototype the shim in go client.
